findings.summary: The duplicate-creation regression test exercises two concurrent runCli calls in one process, so it does not prove the intended cross-process CLI serialization behavior.
findings.broken_invariant: The approved contract requires coverage of concurrent duplicate creation, and the evaluator stop rule permits pass only when concurrency-sensitive paths are covered. The implementation introduces a filesystem transaction specifically capable of coordinating separate processes, but the frozen test evidence only invokes Promise.all over two calls sharing one runtime.

evidence_refs.section: run-cli.core.tasks.create.test.ts concurrent duplicate test and new.ts creation transaction

missing_tests: Spawn two independent task create CLI processes against the same repository and outcome, synchronize their start, and assert exactly one task is persisted while the other exits with the duplicate-validation result; also assert the persisted execution_route remains frozen and consistent.
hidden_assumptions: withTaskReadmeTransaction provides correct mutual exclusion across independent operating-system processes, not only concurrent calls within one JavaScript runtime.
recovery_context: Add deterministic cross-process duplicate-creation coverage for the filesystem transaction, then rerun the declared verification contract and record the result against the same implementation behavior.
